parts.prompt_markdown: Find the velocity of the particle during the last 20 s of its motion.
Sketch a velocity-time graph for the motion of the particle from \(t = 0\) to \(t = 60\).

assets.description: A displacement-time graph for a particle. The horizontal axis is time \(t\) in seconds and the vertical axis is displacement \(s\) in metres. The graph is piecewise linear with 4 straight line segments, matching the described motion: the particle first moves away from the origin, then continues at constant speed, then remains at rest, then returns to the starting point.

measurements: 2 m s⁻¹ for a period of 10 s
returns to its starting point when t = 60
relationships: The graph consists of 4 straight line segments.
The slope of each segment represents velocity.
A horizontal segment represents zero velocity.

skills: Use displacement-time graph segments to obtain velocities
Construct velocity-time graph from piecewise linear displacement-time data
methods: Read slopes of displacement-time graph to find velocities
Convert each displacement-time segment into corresponding constant-velocity interval on a velocity-time graph

questions.stem_markdown: The displacement of a particle at time \(t\) s after leaving a fixed point \(O\) is \(s\) m. The diagram shows a displacement-time graph which models the motion of the particle. The graph consists of 4 straight line segments. The particle travels 50 m in the first 10 s, then travels at \(2\text{ m s}^{-1}\) for a period of 10 s. The particle then comes to rest for a period of 20 s, before returning to its starting point when \(t = 60\).

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Any explicit expression for the distance, e.g. $$\frac{x-50}{20-10} = 2 \rightarrow x = 2(20-10) + 50$$.
Oe. Ft *their* distance ≠ 50. Must be negative. Do not ISW if (e.g.) velocity = 3.5. Do allow “3.5 m s⁻¹, directed towards O.”
May be seen on diagram.
Stepped diagram with four horizontal lines segments. Ignore vertical line segments.

All correct. 10, 20, 40 and 60 indicated on the t-axis. *Their* 5, 2 and *their* –3.5 (allow –3 and –4 is acceptable too with line segment halfway between them) indicated on the v-axis, corresponding to the position of the horizontal line segments. FT *their* –3.5 m s⁻¹ and/or FT their 5 m s⁻¹. If their answer to (a) is positive, allow use of negative their answer for this mark.

parts.prompt_markdown: Find the speed of projection of the particle.
Find the distance travelled by the particle between the two times at which its speed is \(10\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

skills: Use given speed at a time to find initial speed
Apply constant acceleration to find time differences
Use kinematics to calculate distance traveled over a speed interval
methods: Use v = u + at to relate upward projection speed to speed at a given time
Use energy/kinematic relations with constant acceleration to find when speed equals a value and compute distance over that time interval

questions.stem_markdown: A particle is projected vertically upwards from horizontal ground. The speed of the particle 2 seconds after it is projected is \(5\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and it is travelling downwards.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $$-5 = u - g \times 2$$ or $$5 = u + g \times 2$$ or $$5 = 0 + gt \Rightarrow t = 0.5$$, so time to greatest height is $$T = 2 - 0.5 = 1.5$$. Hence $$0 = u + (-g) \times 1.5$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For use of constant acceleration to get an equation in $$u$$ only. Using $$v = -5$$, $$t = 2$$ and $$a = \pm g$$.
Must be positive.

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: $$0^2 = 10^2 - 2gs \quad [\Rightarrow s = 5]$$ or $$10^2 = [0^2 + 2]gs \quad [\Rightarrow s = 5]$$ or $$10 = 0 + gt \Rightarrow t = 1$$, so $$s = 10 \times 1 - \frac{1}{2}g \times 1^2 \quad [\Rightarrow s = 5]$$ or $$\frac{1}{2}(m) \times 10^2 = (m)gh \quad [\Rightarrow h = 5]$$
mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: For use of constant acceleration formula(e) to find distance travelled from height with speed $$10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$$ to maximum height with speed $$0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$$, $$a = \pm g$$. Must be a complete method, e.g. $$0^2 = (\text{their } 15)^2 - 2gs_1 \quad [\Rightarrow s_1 = 11.25]$$ and $$10^2 = (\text{their } 15)^2 - 2gs_2 \quad [\Rightarrow s_2 = 6.25]$$ or $$10 = (\text{their } 15) - gt \quad [\Rightarrow t = 0.5]$$, $$s_2 = \frac{1}{2}(\text{their } 15 + 10) \times (\text{their } 0.5)$$ and with an attempt at $$s_1 - s_2 = 5$$. Energy method with 2 terms, dimensionally correct.
FT $$\text{their } 15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$$ if used.

questions.stem_markdown: A crate of mass 600 kg is being pulled up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane at a constant speed of \(2\text{ m s}^{-1}\) by a rope attached to a winch. The plane is inclined at an angle of \(30^\circ\) to the horizontal and the rope is parallel to the plane. The winch is working at a constant rate of 8 kW.\n\nFind the coefficient of friction between the crate and the plane.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Use of $$F = \frac{P}{v}$$, oe. E.g. $$DF \times 2 = 8000$$.
For attempt to resolve parallel to the plane; 3 terms; allow sign errors; allow sin/cos mix; allow $$g$$ missing; $$F$$ not resolved. Allow with just DF.
To form an equation in $$\mu$$ only where $$R$$ is a component of weight or mass.

The directions of the forces are as shown in the diagram.\n\nGiven that the forces are in equilibrium, find the value of \(F\) and the value of \(\theta\).

questions.stem_markdown:
A particle moves in a straight line starting from a point \(O\). The velocity \(v	ext{ m s}^{-1}\) of the particle \(t\) s after leaving \(O\) is given by

$$v = t^3 -  rac{9}{2}t^2 + 1 	ext{ for } 0 \leq t \leq 4.$$

You may assume that the velocity of the particle is positive for \(t <  rac{1}{2}\), is zero at \(t =  rac{1}{2}\) and is negative for \(t >  rac{1}{2}\).

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: Increase power by 1 and a change in coefficient in at least one term (which must be the same term). $$s = vt$$ is M0.
May be unsimplified.
Use limits 0 and $$\frac{1}{2}$$ correctly, or substitute $$t = \frac{1}{2}$$. M0 if including other regions.
Decrease power by 1 and a change in coefficient in at least one term (which must be the same term). $$a = \frac{v}{t}$$ is M0.
Ignore $$t = 0$$ if not rejected.

Must be using an expression for s from integration. Allow missing minus sign at start; use limits $$\frac{1}{2}$$ and their 3 correctly, where $$\frac{1}{2} < \text{their } 3 \le 4$$. Or use limit 3 and find difference from $$\text{their } \frac{21}{64}$$ from part (a). May see $$2 \times \left( \frac{1}{4} \times \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^4 - \frac{3}{2} \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^3 + \left( \frac{1}{2} \right) \right) - \left( \frac{1}{4} \times 3^4 - \frac{3}{2} \times 3^3 + 3 \right)$$

parts.prompt_markdown: It is given that \(F = 100\). Find the acceleration of the car and the tension in the tow-bar.

It is given instead that the total work done against \(F\) in moving a distance of 50 m up the road is 6000 J. The speed of the car at the start of the 50 m is \(20\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Use an energy method to find the speed of the car at the end of the 50 m.

skills: Resolve forces up the incline
Apply Newton’s second law to find acceleration and tow-bar tension
Use energy/work to relate change in kinetic energy to work against resistances and gravity component
methods: Use F=ma with forces parallel to the plane and tension as an internal force to find acceleration
Use work-energy: change in kinetic energy equals work done by the engine minus work against resistances (including gravity component through sin α)

The car and trailer are connected by a tow-bar which is light and rigid and is parallel to the road. There is a resistance force of 800 N acting on the car and a resistance force of \(F\text{ N}\) acting on the trailer. The driving force of the car's engine is 3000 N.

Any two equations correct.

parts.prompt_markdown: Verify that particle \(P\) reaches \(B\) 0.5 s after it is released, with speed \(3\text{ m s}^{-1}\).
Find the time that it takes from the instant the two particles are released until they collide.
Find the time that it takes from the instant the particles collide until the combined particle reaches \(C\).

The lengths \(AB = 0.75\text{ m}\) and \(BC = 3.25\text{ m}\) are shown, together with the angle \(\theta\). The section \(AB\) is smooth and the section \(BC\) is rough.

relationships: The plane ABC is inclined at an angle θ to the horizontal.
Particles P and Q move along the line of greatest slope of the plane.

skills: Compute motion time and speed on smooth/rough sections using constant acceleration

questions.stem_markdown:
The diagram shows two particles \(P\) and \(Q\) which lie on a line of greatest slope of a plane \(ABC\). Particles \(P\) and \(Q\) are each of mass \(m\) kg. The plane is inclined at an angle \(\theta\) to the horizontal, where \(\sin \theta = 0.6\). The length of \(AB\) is \(0.75\text{ m}\) and the length of \(BC\) is \(3.25\text{ m}\). The section \(AB\) of the plane is smooth and the section \(BC\) is rough. The coefficient of friction between each particle and the section \(BC\) is 0.25. Particle \(P\) is released from rest at \(A\). At the same instant, particle \(Q\) is released from rest at \(B\).

The two particles coalesce when they collide. The coefficient of friction between the combined particle and the plane is still 0.25.
